pageData.heading: The Home Buying Process (Legal & Documentation)
pageData.para: Buying a home is not just about choosing the right property and securing financing—it’s also about getting the legal and documentation process right. This page will guide you through the essential paperwork, verification steps, and common legal pitfalls to ensure a smooth and hassle-free home-buying experience.

laws.heading: Understanding Legal Due Diligence Before Buying a Home
subPara: Before making any commitment, it's crucial to legally verify the property to ensure there are no hidden disputes or liabilities.
Key Legal Checks Before Purchase :
paraGraph: Title Verification – Ensure the seller has a clear and marketable title to the property.
Encumbrance Certificate (EC) – Confirms the property is free from any outstanding loans or legal claims.
Sale Agreement & Sale Deed – The agreement states the terms of the sale, while the deed officially transfers ownership.
Property Tax Receipts – Check if the property has any pending tax dues.
RERA Registration – If it’s a new project, verify if it’s registered under RERA (Real Estate Regulatory Authority).
Approval from Local Authorities – Ensure the property has legal approvals from the municipal corporation and development authorities.
Land Use & Zoning Clearance – Confirms whether the property is approved for residential purposes.
bottomPara: 💡 Pro Tip: Always get a legal expert to verify property documents before making any payment.

contents.heading: Essential documents you need to provide for a home loan
contents.para: Once you finalize the property, you need to submit various documents to the bank for loan approval.

list.heading: For salaried buyers
desc: Income proof (salary slips of last 3 months, Form 16)
Employment proof (offer letter or experience letter)

list.heading: Property-related documents required for a loan​
desc: Sale agreement & allotment letter (for under-construction property)
Approved building plan & property tax receipts

document.proTip: 💡 Pro Tip: Keeping these documents ready can speed up the home loan approval process by 5-7 working days!

charges.para1: Apart from the property price and home loan, you also need to pay stamp duty & registration charges, which vary by state.
charges.proTip: 💡 Pro Tip: If you register the property in a woman’s name, many states offer a lower stamp duty rate (1%-2% discount), helping you save lakhs!

possession.heading: The Final Registration & Possession Process
subPara: Once your loan is approved and the payment is processed, you must register the property in your name at the local sub-registrar’s office.
paraGraph: Step 1: Pay the stamp duty and registration fees.
Step 2: Sign the Sale Deed in the presence of a registrar.
Step 3: Get the document verified and signed by witnesses.
Step 4: Collect the registered Sale Deed after processing (usually within a week).
bottomPara: 💡 Pro Tip: After registration, don’t forget to update property records in your name at the municipal office to avoid tax issues later.

pitfalls.para: Even experienced buyers make mistakes when dealing with legal and financial aspects of home buying. Here’s how you can avoid them:
bullets: Buying without title verification – Always check legal ownership history.
Not checking hidden charges in builder agreements – Read every clause carefully.
Ignoring project approvals – Ensure the builder has received clearance from local authorities.
Skipping RERA verification – Always buy from RERA-registered projects.
Not calculating total costs (stamp duty, GST, maintenance fees) – Budget for all costs upfront.
pitfalls.proTip: 💡 Pro Tip: : If a deal looks “too good to be true,” double-check the legal paperwork before proceeding.

cardData.para:
• Ensure all property documents are legally verified.
  • Keep home loan paperwork ready for quick processing.
  • Pay stamp duty & registration charges as per state laws.
  • Cross-check property handover conditions with the builder/seller.
  • Update municipal records in your name after purchase.
